title: Cash Conversion & Working Capital
question: Where could collection and inventory changes release cash?
method: Compute FY2025 DSO/DIO/DPO using average FY2024/FY2025 balances and a standardized 365-day convention. DSO uses total sales; DIO and DPO use total cost of sales as a proxy for purchases. Scenario reduces DSO by five days and DIO by three, with DPO unchanged. Translate days into a one-time cash release at FY2025 sales/cost levels.
result: The simplified cash conversion cycle is -71.8 days. The stated improvement scenario releases $7.52bn once, not recurring profit.
limits: Vendor non-trade receivables are excluded. Total COGS includes services and is an imperfect inventory/purchases denominator. Credit sales and purchase volumes are unavailable. The scenario is a sensitivity, not an operational recommendation.

title: Profitability & Capital Budgeting
question: How can reported margins inform a clearly bounded investment case?
method: Calculate reported Products and Services gross margins. Separately model a hypothetical five-year project with initial spend equal to 1% of FY2025 reported capex, annual after-tax cash inflow equal to 30% of that spend, 10% discount rate, no terminal value and no additional working capital. Compute NPV, bisection IRR and a 3×3 discount-rate/cash-flow sensitivity.
result: Reported product gross margin is 36.77% versus 75.41% for services. The hypothetical project NPV is $0.02bn and IRR 15.24%.
limits: Gross margin is not contribution margin: public COGS does not separate variable and fixed costs. No SKU break-even is claimed. Project inflows, discount rate and life are assumptions; only the scale anchor comes from real capex. This is not an actual Apple project.
